title: Check yourself: what the server's log can tell you

questions.stem: A new participant, VelocityCheck, extends org.jpos.util.Log and writes one event per transaction with its reasons. In production its descriptor element is <participant class="com.example.VelocityCheck" realm="velocity">. The TransactionManager runs with debug on and debug-context off. VelocityCheck refuses a purchase. What does the server's log hold from VelocityCheck?

options.text: Its event, under the realm velocity, since the element's realm attribute is where the participant logs
options.says: the factory calls setLogger, with the realm, only when the element has a logger attribute

options.text: Its event, inside the TransactionManager's event, since with debug on the TransactionManager collects participant events
options.says: the TransactionManager's event lists votes and timings; a participant's events are separate, and need a logger

options.text: Nothing from it, since the element names no logger, and an event from a Log without one goes nowhere
options.says: without logger the factory never calls setLogger, and an event from a Log with no logger is dropped silently

options.text: Nothing from it, since debug-context is off, and participant events are printed as part of the Context dump
options.says: that is ctx.log; a participant's own events don't depend on debug-context, only on having a logger

origin.section: 8.2 A Participant Writes Its Own Event, and Only If Its Element Names a Logger

questions.stem: A participant reads a card table. When the query throws an SQLException, it catches it, calls ctx.log(e), puts a 96 response in the Context and votes ABORTED. It writes no event of its own. The logger has ProtectedLogListener first; the TransactionManager has debug on and debug-context off. The table goes offline for ten minutes. Where can an operator read those SQLExceptions?

options.text: In a warn event from the TransactionManager, since with debug on it logs every exception its participants run into
options.says: the TransactionManager logs a warn only for an exception that escapes prepare; this one was caught

options.text: In the TransactionManager's event for each transaction, since ctx.log adds a line under the participant's vote
options.says: the event lists votes and timings; ctx.log writes into the Context, which the event leaves out

options.text: Nowhere in the log, since ProtectedLogListener drops exceptions that might carry card data
options.says: the filter masks ISOMsg fields and leaves other entries alone; it drops nothing

options.text: Nowhere in the log, since ctx.log writes into the Context, which is printed only in its dump
options.says: with debug-context off the Context dump is off, so what ctx.log collected is never written

origin.section: 8.1 The Transaction Event Says Who Voted, Never Why

questions.stem: A participant marks its three steps with ctx.checkPoint("..."). The TransactionManager has profiler on and debug-context off. The participant's prepare takes about 900 ms. What does the TransactionManager's profiler show for that participant?

options.text: Only the participant's line, since checkpoints go to a profiler kept in the Context, printed only in its dump
options.says: ctx.checkPoint writes to the Context's profiler, printed only with the Context dump

options.text: Only the participant's line, since checkpoints are printed only when the participant also writes an event of its own
options.says: a participant's own event doesn't print the Context's profiler; checkpoints need the Context dump

options.text: A line per step after the participant's line, since checkpoints are added to the TransactionManager's profiler
options.says: the TransactionManager's profiler is its own; ctx.checkPoint never reaches it

options.text: A line per step in place of the participant's line, since checkpoints split the participant's time into parts
options.says: the TransactionManager's line for the participant is unchanged, and the steps don't appear at all

origin.section: 8.4 The TransactionManager Times Participants; a Profiler of Your Own Times the Steps

questions.stem: A server runs four sessions. At 14:00 the TransactionManager's events show tail=812. At 14:05 they still show tail=812, while head has gone from 840 to 1310, and paused stays at 0. What does that say about transaction 812?

options.text: It is waiting in the queue for a session, since tail is the oldest Context no session has taken yet
options.says: Contexts waiting in the queue are counted by outstanding; tail is the oldest transaction that hasn't finished

options.text: It is still running in a participant, since tail is the oldest transaction that hasn't finished
options.says: head moves with every new transaction while tail stays at the one that never ended

options.text: Nothing about it, since tail only moves when the TransactionManager is restarted
options.says: tail moves every time the oldest unfinished transaction finishes

options.text: Nothing about it, since tail is the first id handed out since the last restart
options.says: tail is the oldest unfinished id; on an idle server it equals head

origin.section: 8.5 A Transaction That Never Ends Writes Nothing, and the Ones After It Show Where It Is
